scope: Failed publication recovery only; ordinary converged application deployments already avoid host configuration.

observed_failure.reason: main advanced; retry reconciliation at its current revision
observed_failure.hosts: All seven hosts completed successfully; no failed or unreachable hosts.

reuse_requirements: Durable publish checkpoint has valid differing desired/applied revisions and positive finite plan, expand, and hosts durations.
Checkpoint is no older than 90 minutes and not future-dated.
Previous desired revision to current source selects no infrastructure or Ansible changes.
Fresh saved expansion plan proves existing resources and outputs unchanged, with no drift, imports, moves, deferred work, or uncertain checks.
preserved: Full pending selection from applied revision

validation.command: GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go test -c ./internal/reconcile -o /tmp/infra-reconcile-checkpoint-tests; scp binary to ntnu; ssh ntnu timeout 15s /tmp/infra-reconcile-checkpoint-tests -test.timeout 10s

validation.fixture: Local terraform_data; no cloud access; applied saved no-op and changed plans accepted and rejected respectively.

failure_coverage: Explicit full request and incomplete or expired checkpoints rerun hosts.
Changed, malformed, or unreadable expansion proofs rerun hosts.
Errors in every retained stage still fail reconciliation.
Cancellation stops subsequent work and releases the state lock.
A failed resumed publication does not invent a completed hosts duration for another reuse.

independent_review.result: No blocking findings; targeted resume and host-reuse tests passed.

limitations: No production latency result or percentile is claimed.
The 0.20-second fixture result is a correctness check, not a deployment benchmark.
Manual host configuration drift retains existing incremental reconciliation semantics; explicit full requests always rerun host configuration.
